newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah jolted briefly on Suharto health.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah jolted briefly on Suharto health.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was jolted briefly against the dollar on renewed rumours over President Suharto's health at mid-afternoon on Thursday, dealers said.
They said there were rumours that Suharto was sick, but the presidential palace denied this.
"The president has had a full programme today and is fine," a palace official said.
Dealers said it was not clear who started the rumours.
Some said it came from Singapore while others said it came from Jakarta. Dealers said the rumours triggered off some nervous dollar selling to a high of 2,376.0/77.0.
But some foreign bank dealers said the dollar buying had started in Jakarta.

Indonesian financial markets were jittery last July over the news that Suharto had travelled to Europe for medical checks. But the markets recovered quickly after Suharto was given a clean bill of health.
Liquidity seemed to tighten slightly in the afternoon, helping overnight money recover to 8.5 percent and three-day tom/next swaps to inch up to 1.25 points.
"Somebody seemed to have intentionally created the rumours as we can see there was not enough power to drive the dollar up strongly," one local bank dealer said.
"The market seemed to have been able to digest the rumours pretty quickly and countered back," he said.
Spot rupiah settled at 2,374.0/75.0 at 0845 GMT against an opening of 2,371.25/71.75. Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,373.0/74.0 and 2,372.75/73.25, respectively.
The local bank dealer said the rumours seemed to be from Singapore because some players were long there.
"It's a good opportunity to cash out," he said.
The rupiah weakened in the morning partly due to excess liquidity while others attributed to possible spillover from Thailand which was hit by devaluation rumours.
Bank Indonesia raised its intervention band by one point to 2,369/2.561 and the conversion band to 2,369/2,417 on Thursday.
It was the second rise this week after depreciating the rupiah by four points last week.
One-month swaps were at 11.50/12.00, two at 22.00/22.50, three at 33.50/34.25 and six at 71.25/72.00 points.
